## portcheck monitor add

Add a monitor

### Synopsis

Add a URL (http or https) or a TCP address to monitor, and check it once.

A URL is up when it answers within --timeout with a status in --status
(default 200-299, after redirects) and, with --contains, a body containing
that text. An address is up when it accepts a connection. A bare port means
localhost.

```
portcheck monitor add <url|host:port|port> [flags]
```

### Examples

```
  portcheck monitor add https://example.com/health
  portcheck monitor add https://api.example.com/ping --every 30s --contains pong
  portcheck monitor add db.internal:5432 --name postgres --every 5m
```

### Options

```
      --contains string   text the response must contain, e.g. pong
      --every string      how often to check, at least 10s (default 1m)
  -h, --help              help for add
      --name string       name in lists and alerts (default: the URL without https://, or the address)
      --status string     HTTP statuses that count as up, e.g. 200-399 or 200,204 (default 200-299)
      --timeout string    how long one check may take (default 10s)
```

### Options inherited from parent commands

```
      --json                shorthand for --output json
      --log-format string   log format: text or json (default "text")
      --no-color            disable colors (also honors NO_COLOR)
  -o, --output string       output format: table, plain, csv, json (default: table on a terminal, plain otherwise)
  -v, --verbose             log diagnostic details to stderr
```
